stories.title: One month until Vaping Products Duty and Vaping Duty Stamps Scheme start
stories.summary: HMRC has reminded businesses across the vaping supply chain — including retailers and wholesalers — to prepare for the new Vaping Products Duty and Vaping Duty Stamps Scheme launching on 1 October 2026.

stories.title: Revenue and Customs Brief 9 (2026): VAT liability of supplies of education by alternative providers
stories.summary: HMRC published a new Revenue and Customs Brief clarifying the VAT treatment of education supplies by alternative providers of higher and further education, effective from 2 September 2026.

stories.title: Government, police and music industry unite to tackle VAWG
stories.summary: A joint initiative between the government, police forces and the music industry has been announced to tackle Violence Against Women and Girls (VAWG), with new commitments targeting safer environments at festivals and live events.

stories.title: PM accelerates roll out of police rape and sexual offence specialist teams
stories.summary: The Prime Minister has brought forward by 18 months the deadline for all police forces in England and Wales to have specialist rape and sexual offence investigation teams in place, stepping up action on Violence Against Women and Girls.

stories.title: Small boat activity in the English Channel — transparency data updated
stories.summary: The Home Office published its latest transparency data on migrants detected crossing the English Channel in small boats, as Parliament returned from summer recess.

stories.title: UK accelerates support for efforts to stop Ebola outbreak at source
stories.summary: The UK's Africa Minister Kirsty McNeill announced a £50 million package to combat the growing Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, bringing the total UK contribution to £78 million. The DRC outbreak is on course to become the deadliest Ebola epidemic ever recorded.

stories.title: £13m to turn cutting-edge research into real-world farming solutions
stories.summary: Environment Secretary Dame Angela Eagle launched the latest round of the Farming Innovation Programme, with £13 million in grants (£1–3m per project) to help researchers, farmers and agri-tech businesses develop practical tools — from AI-powered robotic tomato harvesters to new vaccines protecting pigs from disease.

stories.title: £30 million Farmer Collaboration Fund opens for applications
stories.summary: Alongside the Farming Innovation Programme announcement, applications opened for a new £30 million Farmer Collaboration Fund to help farmers and land managers work together to cut costs, share knowledge and build resilience — part of a £200 million agricultural innovation commitment by 2030.

stories.title: UK military still targets 3% of GDP on defence by 2030 despite timeline pressure
stories.summary: The UK military is maintaining its expectation that defence spending will reach 3% of GDP by 2030, even after delays in the Chancellor's commitments. The OBR has estimated this goal would cost roughly £15 billion per year — equivalent to a 2% rise in basic income tax.

stories.title: RAF Air Command renamed Air & Space Command
stories.summary: The Royal Air Force's Air Command headquarters has been renamed Air & Space Command, reflecting the RAF's expanding role in space operations and the growing importance of satellite-based military capabilities.

stories.title: Architect of UK government's AI strategy joins Anthropic
stories.summary: Matt Clifford, who drafted the UK's AI Action Plan and advised both PM Starmer and former PM Sunak, has joined US AI firm Anthropic as Managing Director for International Affairs. The move has prompted debate about the 'revolving door' between government and the tech industry.

stories.title: 12 new experts appointed to CMA's inquiry panel
stories.summary: The Department for Business, Innovation, Science and Trade (DBIST) has appointed 12 new independent members to the Competition and Markets Authority's inquiry panel, bringing expertise in economics, finance, law and technology to support the CMA's work on mergers, market investigations and regulatory appeals.

stories.title: Oxfordshire science facilities protected from funding cuts
stories.summary: Oxfordshire's major science research facilities — operated by the Science and Technology Facilities Council (STFC) — have been protected from the worst of potential funding cuts, though STFC's budget will still reduce by 15% over four years through efficiency savings.

stories.title: Harrogate NHS Trust becomes first to use AI for breast cancer HER2 diagnosis
stories.summary: Harrogate and District NHS Foundation Trust has deployed the UK's first AI-enabled HER2 tissue scanning system in clinical use, funded by £40,000 from charity. The Roche scanner uses AI algorithms to help pathologists assess HER2 status in breast cancer patients faster, enabling earlier treatment decisions.

stories.title: Gaps in NHS end-of-life care 'denying ill children chance to die at home'
stories.summary: A Guardian investigation has found significant gaps in NHS end-of-life care for children, with families reporting that inadequate at-home support is forcing terminally ill children to spend their final days in hospital rather than at home.

stories.title: NHS England launches consultation on statistical publications reform
stories.summary: NHS England has opened a public consultation on reforming how it publishes statistical data, proposing new, more accessible ways to view NHS summary data, indicators and measures while reviewing existing statistics publications.

stories.title: Bath's only city centre Post Office branch closes
stories.summary: Bath's only city centre Post Office branch has closed, with the Post Office saying it hopes to open a replacement branch as soon as possible. The closure leaves a significant gap in postal services for the city centre.

stories.title: Hanley postbox still out of action three months after vehicle collision
stories.summary: A Royal Mail postbox in Hanley's Market Square remains out of service three months after being struck by a vehicle, frustrating local residents and shoppers who rely on it.
